content: Metabolic surgery should be considered for adolescents diagnosed with type 2 diabetes who also have severe obesity. Severe obesity is defined as a body mass index (BMI) greater than 35 kg/m² or at least 120% of the 95th percentile for age and sex, whichever threshold is lower. This intervention is appropriate when serious comorbidities are present and when lifestyle modifications and pharmacologic treatments have failed to achieve adequate results. Such surgical procedures should only be performed in specialized medical centers equipped with a multidisciplinary team. This team should include surgeons, endocrinologists, dietitians, and behavioral health specialists to ensure comprehensive care and optimal outcomes. Research has demonstrated that metabolic surgery can result in substantial weight loss, improved glycemic control, and even remission of diabetes in some cases. However, further studies are necessary to fully understand the long-term effects and outcomes of this intervention.
